newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut unemployment at 5.2 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut unemployment at 5.2 pct in June.

text.p: Connecticut Department of Labor reported on Wednesday nonfarm jobs increased between May and June while the unemployment rate held steady at 5.2 percent .

Nonfarm jobs have increased by 28,000 since June 1996. The unemployment rate was down half a precent point from June 1996, and was two-tenths of a precent point above the national rate of 5.0 percent.

Job gains were reported in wholesale and retail trade, up 2,900;services, up 1,600;construction and mining, up 900;manufacturing, up 800; transportation, communications and utilities, up 500; and finance, insurance and real estate, up 200. A decrease was reported in government, down 900.
In June , an estimated 91,400 Connecticut residents were unemployed. That number was up from May's figure, and down 5,800 from June 1996.

"June's nonfarm employment represented the best May-June gain since 1984, reflecting strong summer hiring," said Salvatore DiPillo, labor statistics supervisor. "Hiring might have been stronger if not for laboe shortages experienced in some parts of the state."
